fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "What Synchromysticism Actually Means", "body": "Chance Garton opens by admitting the word synchromystic gets thrown around without definition, then quotes a description of it as part artistic practice, part metaphysical system and part conspiracy culture. Mike Wann breaks the term in half. The mysticism is the baseline conviction that everything is one big ball of wax with nothing sitting outside the whole. The synchronicity half is the practical use of meaningful coincidence as a compass for navigating reality. His personal flavor adds pop culture, especially film, and casting yourself as the main character in your own unfolding story."}, {"title": "Conspiracy As Training For The Mind", "body": "Mike Wann defends conspiracy research not as a body of facts but as a curriculum. Because reality is a self fulfilling prophecy realm running on beliefs, and beliefs are ultimately narratives, the first conspiracy that upends what you were taught teaches you how flexible narratives really are. That flexibility is the skill worth keeping. He also warns about the failure mode he calls the James Shelby Downard spiral, the paranoid conviction that everything is connected and everyone is out to get you. He defends Wikipedia too, as a fast map of what the collective is meant to believe."}, {"title": "Kronos, Kyrios And The 33 Nights", "body": "Chance Garton introduces the two Greek words for time. Kronos is measured clock time, which he calls fake, and Kyrios is subjective time measured by your own development. Mike Wann says the 33 nights on the road felt far more expansive than a month at home doing the same things, because physical distance and novelty stretched his memory out of alignment with the calendar. He tracks time by the moon and by his starboard ceremonies instead. Chance suggests the dilation of time is driven by story, and that novelty is how you jump the fence on Kronos."}, {"title": "The Freemason Talk That Killed Mike Wann", "body": "In December 2021 Mike Wann was invited to present his Susquehanna research to a lodge of Freemasons near Philadelphia. He found six encoded links between the invitation and his own presentation on the Kobe Bryant helicopter crash, including the date and the location tied to Bryant's high school. Rather than back out he told the drunk room that this was an initiation between himself and the universe and that they were his witnesses. The next day his relationship and his settled life collapsed. Chance Garton reframes it plainly, saying the Mike Wann of that moment was the sacrifice."}, {"title": "Rivers, Forrest Gump And The Arrow", "body": "The trip began ceremonially, with three bottles of Susquehanna River water poured into every major river along the way and local water collected in exchange. Then Hollywood started answering back. Santa Monica Pier on July 4th put them in Richard Kelly's Southland Tales, a Bubba Gump meal seeded Forrest Gump, and the Madrid anthracite coal that fed Los Alamos landed them there the weekend Christopher Nolan's Oppenheimer opened. Mike Wann ties it to Peter Kingsley's book A Story Waiting to Pierce You and Abaris the arrow circulator, and to the arrow he built ten years earlier without knowing why."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The original Susquehanna Sage, Mike Wann, returns to InnerVerse! Last month I was blessed with an in-person visit with the uniquely mystical man himself, as part of his coast-to-coast magical summer roadtrip. As we've come to expect from Mike, his journey is riddled with, well, riddles, as the events in the media and his own divergent discoveries meshed together in a fractal expression of the great cosmic script of consciousness. In this episode, the master story-teller will unpack some of the mysteries he uncovered on his path from Pennsylvania to California and back.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Hexagram That Changes Mid Conversation", "body": "Back from the intermission, Chance reveals that the coins he threw before the show produced changing lines, so hexagram 33, Retreat, is shifting into 31, which is called Influence. Both of them read it as the eros card, and they take care to qualify that it is not narrowly sexual but a matter of magnetic charge and connection between people. Mike then explains why he keeps casting himself as the main character of his own stories, calling it a fine line to walk and framing the whole practice as a demonstration that reality is far more malleable than he ever imagined it could be."}, {"title": "A Firstborn Mind And A Friendly Universe", "body": "Chance lays out a long thought experiment. If the pleroma is everything and its opposites at once, could a first separate mind emanate from it, and would that mind want to keep the rest of us from getting stuck in loops that amount to a hell? He ties it to the savior archetype and asks whether the arrow really works as a passport between realms. Mike declines the metaphysics. He says he does not know the nature of this reality and does not think he can know it, then offers the question he attributes to Einstein, whether this is a friendly universe or a dangerous one."}, {"title": "Good Guys, Bad Guys And Demon Corp", "body": "Mike admits he has spent weeks asking whether the CIA is really what he assumed it was, whether the hands staging the rise and fall of civilizations are villains or something stranger, and he points to the Rosicrucians as a tradition that always played that pun on itself. Chance carries it into the underworld, noting that demonia in Greek means the spirits of dead humans rather than infernal outsiders, and sketching what he calls demon corp, a ranked and trained hierarchy of hungry ghosts who get assigned rather than stumbled into. His closing question is whether the intelligence doing the winking also runs that operation."}, {"title": "Energy As A Compass For Saying No", "body": "Chance tells a story he says he can only tell in the private hour. He was offered a slot in an online summit promising enormous exposure, but the contract read as punitive and the organizer's name turned out to be a fairly easy anagram for a hall of mirrors. His energy kept tanking as the recording date approached, and the moment he sent the email declining, it came flooding back. Mike answers with the opposite instinct, describing himself as a homebody who often has to eat his vegetables and go do the thing he resists. Between them they land on reading resistance rather than obeying it."}, {"title": "The Unastrologer On Twelve Borrowed Archetypes", "body": "Mike walks through the star board, the direction aligned chart he builds from an ephemeris and stones so that what sits on the board matches what is actually overhead. Then he turns unastrologer, arguing that we created astrology and it simply reflects us back, which is why so many contradictory systems all work. Chance answers the tropical and sidereal question by pointing at plants that bloom on the solstice regardless of precession. Mike closes on Babylon, the civilization that also handed us banking and class systems, and on how completely twelve archetypes have colonized what we can even picture a person being."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "It's a really fine line you walk when you do the sort of storytelling which I like to do because the stories are about me.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If that's the top level, if that's the beyond beyond, where everything else is emanating from, is it a reasonable philosophical question that a mind emanating from that, a first separate mind could exist?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We wouldn't have as many nerve endings that felt good unless we're supposed to be having some fun.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "They're saying that someday, exactly this conversation will happen again, exactly like it's happening right now.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "At the end of the day, I'm optimistic as can be. I think this is meant to be fun and a game.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Look for where your resistance is at and ask yourself about those areas where you have resistance.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I don't know what the planets are, but I know that something magical happens when we begin to bring awareness to it.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We created the astrology, and it just reflects it back to us.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There are plants that know when the summer solstice is, and they bloom on that summer solstice no matter what, even if the precession causes a different schema to be above them at that moment.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Archetypes are a conversation that we are having. They are a language for us to communicate with the universe about what we want and who we want to be.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Synchromisticism has been described as part artistic practice, part spiritual or metaphysical system, parts conspiracy culture and all these components are true. It seems that at the intersection of curiosity and creativity, we can somehow crack the windows into a more pleromic level of existence", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "mystic is an understanding of the interconnectedness of all of life and all of reality, but then utilizing synchronicity or, you know, I guess like the common definition would be a meaningful coincidence as a compass in order to navigate reality.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "To me, that's why conspiracy is so important is like it really trains the mind to begin to look at narratives, to question narratives, to see how narratives can literally change experiential reality to extreme degrees.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "And I really like to point out that in Greek, there's actually two words for time, Kronos being measured time that we go by the clock, the movement of luminaries, but then Kyrios is subjective time, spiritual time, the time that is measured by your own personal development in a sequential way.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And I'm like, what's happening is an initiation between me, Mike Wan and the universe, whoever the universe may be. And you as Freemasons are the ultimate symbols of initiation and you are my witness.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "But the reason why astrology works is because the heavens are our unifier because we all get to see the same moon. We're all under the same sky. We don't all get to see the same river. We don't all get to see the same mountain but we see the same sky.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "And because of that, like, you know, I think that that might actually be the root and the foundation of the entire expansion principle that our economic system is based on. Like the infinite growth paradigm that debt works on is like, you know, when you're in that measured time reality, it's always running out.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "and the idea behind that is like, yes, we're always part of the same like big ball of wax where there's never a moment you're not integrated with reality.", "author": "Mike Wann", "portrait": ""}]
